scope: Corollary 6.16 (Base lattice finiteness) of the manuscript “The height-three chromatic overlap: an explicit filtration and its attachments” (preprints/The-height-three-chromatic-overlap-an-explicit-filtration-and-its-attachments-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 05577ee22db5cad1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 54. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let L be a coefficient line over K whose pullback to L has an H-invariant frame at a finite stage. Suppose that Λ ⊂ L is a P3-stable order lattice over k[[y]]. Then Ha cts(P3, Λ) and Ha cts(H, Λ) are finite for every a. This applies to every periodicity power, every finite determinant character, their inverses, and their products with conormal or canonical-line twists. In particular each adjacent x-pole strip used in Section 8 has finite P3-cohomology.
